rules.quote: Claude reads `MEMORY.md` and follows the linked rule files.
rules.rule: On a fresh machine, read the repo's memory `MEMORY.md` index and follow the rule files it links to.

rules.quote:
treat the sync as a manual step when
new rules land.
rules.rule: Treat syncing memory files between the repo mirror and the auto-memory location as a manual step whenever new rules are written.

rules.quote: every brief MUST assign each agent a distinct, currently-unused port
rules.rule: When dispatching worktree agents that may run a dev server, assign each agent a distinct, currently unused port in its brief.

rules.quote: Pick a range like `3010-3099` for agents
rules.rule: Choose agent dev server ports from a range such as 3010-3099.

rules.quote: avoid `3000-3001` since those are the user's defaults
rules.rule: Do not assign ports 3000 or 3001 to agents.

rules.quote: Each agent brief gets one unique value.
rules.rule: Give each agent brief exactly one unique port value.

rules.quote: Tell the agent how to override the port.
rules.rule: Tell each agent in its brief how to override the dev server port.

rules.quote: verify the convention before the dispatch and bake the exact invocation into the brief
rules.rule: Before dispatching agents, verify the port override convention and include the exact invocation in the brief.

rules.quote: Default the orchestrator's own dev server to a non-3001 port when bringing it up
rules.rule: When starting the orchestrator's own dev server, use a port other than 3001.

rules.quote: For waves with N agents, allocate N+1 ports
rules.rule: For a wave of N agents, allocate N+1 ports, reserving one for the orchestrator's own verification server.

rules.quote: Do NOT use port 3001
rules.rule: Agents must not use port 3001 for their dev servers.

rules.quote: Always note which port belongs to which worktree
rules.rule: Record which dev server port belongs to which worktree.

rules.quote: tear down or replace before re-screenshotting
rules.rule: Before re-screenshotting, tear down or replace any dev server still running from a previous worktree.

rules.quote: they CANNOT all use Playwright
rules.rule: When dispatching parallel worktree agents that need to verify their work, do not have them all use Playwright.

rules.quote: Default agent verification = NOT Playwright.
rules.rule: By default, verify agent work without using Playwright.

rules.quote: `bun run typecheck` (cheap, always available)
rules.rule: Prefer running `bun run typecheck` to verify agent work.

rules.quote: `bun build` (catches loader/transpile errors)
rules.rule: Prefer running `bun build` to verify agent work.

rules.quote: Read the file back
rules.rule: Verify agent work by reading the changed file back.

rules.quote: walk the JSX manually
rules.rule: Verify JSX changes by walking the JSX manually.

rules.quote: reason about layout
rules.rule: Verify layout by reasoning about it instead of opening a browser.

rules.quote: do the math (auto-fit minmax(40, 56) at 230px width = 5 columns of 40-46px = 5 brushes fit, etc.) instead of opening a browser
rules.rule: For dimension or responsive checks, calculate the expected dimensions instead of opening a browser.

rules.quote: Do NOT spawn or use a Playwright session — the orchestrator owns the browser.
rules.rule: Tell each dispatched agent not to spawn or use a Playwright session, because the orchestrator owns the browser.

rules.quote: Verify via typecheck + reasoning only.
rules.rule: Tell each dispatched agent to verify its work via typecheck and reasoning only.

rules.quote: Run that wave **sequentially**, not parallel
rules.rule: When a wave needs Playwright verification per panel, run that wave's agents sequentially, not in parallel.

rules.quote: have the agents emit verification SQL (panel size + visible-element queries)
rules.rule: As an alternative to parallel Playwright use, have agents emit verification SQL queries for panel size and visible elements.

rules.quote: have the orchestrator run them in batch after the wave lands
rules.rule: Have the orchestrator run agents' verification SQL queries in a batch after the wave lands.

rules.quote: pause the audit until the wave is fully merged
rules.rule: Pause the orchestrator's Playwright audit until the wave is fully merged.

rules.quote: the cleanest fix is to NOT spin up dev servers in the agent at all
rules.rule: Do not have agents spin up dev servers for verification.

rules.quote: rely on the orchestrator's running server post-merge
rules.rule: Rely on the orchestrator's running dev server after merge rather than starting dev servers in agents.

rules.quote: they need distinct ports
rules.rule: If agents do spin up dev servers for verification, give each agent a distinct port.

rules.quote: For any task beyond a trivial one-file edit, **delegate to an Agent subagent**.
rules.rule: For any task beyond a trivial one-file edit, delegate the work to an Agent subagent.

rules.quote: Use Explore for read-only research
rules.rule: Use the Explore subagent for read-only research tasks.

rules.quote: general-purpose (or a Vercel-specific specialist when it matches) for multi-file implementations
rules.rule: Use the general-purpose subagent (or a Vercel-specific specialist when one matches) for multi-file implementations.

rules.quote: The main context exists for orchestration, decisions, and user-facing summaries — not for running greps, reading large source trees, or executing multi-file diffs.
rules.rule: Keep the main context for orchestration, decisions, and user-facing summaries; do not run greps, read large source trees, or execute multi-file diffs directly in it.

rules.quote: Before doing any meaningful read/grep/edit pass, ask "could a subagent do this and report back in under 200 words?" If yes, delegate.
rules.rule: Before doing any meaningful read, grep, or edit pass, ask whether a subagent could do it and report back in under 200 words; if yes, delegate it.

rules.quote: Bundle related work into a single dispatch — don't fragment one logical change across many small agent calls.
rules.rule: Bundle related work into a single subagent dispatch; do not split one logical change across many small agent calls.

rules.quote: The prompt to the subagent must be self-contained (it doesn't see this conversation): include the plan docs to read, the exact file paths, the constraints, and the verification commands.
rules.rule: Make each subagent prompt self-contained, including the plan docs to read, exact file paths, constraints, and verification commands.

rules.quote: For panel polish work, run a two-agent loop per panel
rules.rule: For panel polish work, run a two-agent loop per panel: a thorough audit agent first, then a focused fix agent that acts on the audit findings.

rules.quote: Sequential per panel.
rules.rule: Run the audit-then-fix loop sequentially for each panel, not in parallel across panels.

rules.quote: Orchestrator writes detailed briefs for both.
rules.rule: The orchestrator writes a detailed brief for both the audit agent and the fix agent.

rules.quote: Reports findings — does NOT modify any code.
rules.rule: The audit agent reports findings and must not modify any code.

rules.quote: Output format: a structured findings report — one finding per issue, with screenshot evidence.
rules.rule: The audit agent's output must be a structured findings report with one finding per issue, including screenshot evidence.

rules.quote: Commits + pushes to main directly.
rules.rule: The fix agent commits and pushes its fixes directly to main.

rules.quote: Verifies via Playwright (own tab).
rules.rule: The fix agent verifies its changes via Playwright in its own tab.

rules.quote: Uses Playwright on its own tab to navigate the editor.
rules.rule: The audit agent uses Playwright in its own tab to navigate the editor.

rules.quote: Verifies the panel doesn't break, lose content, scroll horizontally, or render unreadably at any reasonable size.
rules.rule: The audit agent must verify the panel does not break, lose content, scroll horizontally, or render unreadably at any reasonable size.

rules.quote: Validates they match the original intent.
rules.rule: The orchestrator validates audit findings against the original intent before acting on them.

rules.quote: If the fix is solid, marks the panel done.
rules.rule: The orchestrator marks a panel done only after reviewing the fix and confirming it is solid.

rules.quote: - Trivial single-line fixes: just do it directly in the orchestrator.
rules.rule: For trivial single-line fixes, the orchestrator applies the fix directly instead of using the audit-then-fix loop.

rules.quote: Broad sweeps that touch every panel (e.g. "change tooltip timing across all panels"): a single sweep agent or orchestrator-driven sed pattern.
rules.rule: For broad sweeps that touch every panel, use a single sweep agent or an orchestrator-driven sed pattern instead of the per-panel loop.

rules.quote: Building NEW panel content from scratch: a single build agent is fine
rules.rule: When building new panel content from scratch, use a single build agent instead of the audit-then-fix loop.

rules.quote: [[feedback-no-worktrees]] — both audit and fix run in main checkout.
rules.rule: Both audit and fix agents run in the main checkout, not in worktrees.

rules.quote: orchestrator must confirm previous fix is fully merged before starting next panel's audit.
rules.rule: The orchestrator must confirm the previous panel's fix is fully merged before starting the next panel's audit.

rules.quote: audit and fix agents must each open their own Playwright tab.
rules.rule: The audit agent and the fix agent must each open their own Playwright tab.

rules.quote:
Audits are read-only by nature. Dispatch them with
`run_in_background: true` and IMMEDIATELY pick up the next piece of
rules.rule: When dispatching an audit, dispatch it with run_in_background set to true.

rules.quote:
IMMEDIATELY pick up the next piece of
disjoint work (another audit, code edits in non-overlapping files,
doc updates, planning, memory hygiene) without waiting for the audit
to finish.
rules.rule: After dispatching an audit, immediately pick up the next piece of disjoint work (another audit, code edits in non-overlapping files, doc updates, planning, memory hygiene) without waiting for the audit to finish.

rules.quote: ALWAYS parallelize them with other work
rules.rule: Always parallelize audits with other work (another audit, code edits in disjoint files, doc updates, planning).

rules.quote: Never sit idle waiting for an audit to finish.
rules.rule: Never sit idle waiting for an audit to finish.

rules.quote: **When dispatching an audit, immediately decide what comes next**:
rules.rule: When dispatching an audit, immediately decide what comes next.

rules.quote:
Always end an audit-dispatch turn with
  parallel work already in motion.
rules.rule: Always end an audit-dispatch turn with parallel work already in motion.

rules.quote: **Hard avoid**: "the audit is running, I'll wait for the result."
rules.rule: Do not wait for an audit's result while it is running; avoid the stance of 'the audit is running, I'll wait for the result.'

rules.quote:
don't dispatch a FIX agent against the same
  area the audit is auditing — wait for the findings.
rules.rule: Do not dispatch a FIX agent against the same area an audit is auditing; wait for the audit's findings first.

rules.quote:
you CAN
  do other work, including unrelated FIX agents, plan docs,
  refactors in different file trees.
rules.rule: While an audit runs, other work is permitted, including unrelated FIX agents, plan docs, and refactors in different file trees.

rules.quote: Then idle-wait is acceptable.
rules.rule: When audit findings dictate the next step and no other work is queued, idle-waiting for the audit is acceptable.

rules.quote:
check the task list
  first — usually something IS queued.
rules.rule: Before idle-waiting on an audit, check the task list for queued work.

rules.quote: Every new editor action or setting MUST register via registerCommand / registerSetting
rules.rule: Register every new editor action with registerCommand and every new editor setting with registerSetting.

rules.quote: Agent briefs that introduce UI actions or settings must include the registration directive verbatim.
rules.rule: When writing an agent brief that introduces a UI action or setting, include the registration directive verbatim.

rules.quote: Any new action (button click, menu item, keybinding, etc.) MUST be registered via `registerCommand({ id, title, category, keywords?, keybinding?, icon?, run })`
rules.rule: Register every new action (button click, menu item, keybinding, etc.) via registerCommand with id, title, category, and run, and optionally keywords, keybinding, and icon.

rules.quote: Components register from `useEffect(() => registerCommand({...}), [...])` and return the unregister.
rules.rule: Register commands from a component inside a useEffect that returns the unregister function.

rules.quote: Any new user-tunable preference MUST be registered via `registerSetting({ id, title, category, type, default, scope?, ... })`
rules.rule: Register every new user-tunable preference via registerSetting with id, title, category, type, and default, and optionally scope.

rules.quote: Read/write through `useSettingsStore.getState().get(id)` / `.set(id, value)`.
rules.rule: Read and write settings only through useSettingsStore.getState().get(id) and .set(id, value).

rules.quote: Settings reuse the existing source of truth (workspace store, project store, etc.)
rules.rule: Store setting values in the existing source of truth (such as the workspace store or project store), not in new storage.

rules.quote: the registry is the discovery layer, NOT a parallel storage system.
rules.rule: Do not use the settings registry as a separate storage system.

rules.quote: Categories: 'File' / 'Edit' / 'View' / 'Workspace' / 'Navigation' / 'Help'
rules.rule: Assign each registered command one of these categories: 'File', 'Edit', 'View', 'Workspace', 'Navigation', or 'Help'.

rules.quote: The button or menu handler that owns the action's existing UX MUST still work
rules.rule: Keep the existing button or menu handler for an action working when registering that action.

rules.quote: `registerCommand`'s `run` just CALLS the same handler.
rules.rule: Make a registered command's run function call the existing button or menu handler.

rules.quote: Don't create parallel implementations.
rules.rule: Do not create a second implementation of an action that already has a handler.

rules.quote: When in doubt, register it.
rules.rule: When unsure whether an action or setting should be registered, register it.

rules.quote: When the next step is clear, just dispatch and report in a one-line voice update.
rules.rule: When the next step is clear, dispatch immediately and report the dispatch in a one-line voice update.

rules.quote: Don't ask "say go" or "approve the brief?" before launching agents.
rules.rule: Do not ask the user for approval (e.g., "say go" or "approve the brief?") before launching agents.

rules.quote: Dispatch immediately when the decision is clear.
rules.rule: Dispatch immediately when the decision is clear, without pausing for approval.

rules.quote: Continue to confirm only when the call is genuinely ambiguous
rules.rule: Seek confirmation from the user only when the dispatch decision is genuinely ambiguous.

rules.quote: Routine briefs and panel picks just go.
rules.rule: Routine agent briefs and panel picks should be dispatched without seeking approval.

rules.quote: Never sit idle waiting for the user when no agent is working.
rules.rule: Never sit idle waiting for the user when no agent is working.

rules.quote: schedule a self-wakeup 15 min out
rules.rule: When no agent is working and you would otherwise stop to ask the user something, schedule a self-wakeup 15 minutes out.

rules.quote: Check: is at least one agent in flight?
rules.rule: Before stopping to ask the user something, check whether at least one agent is in flight.

rules.quote: standing by is fine; the work continues.
rules.rule: If at least one agent is in flight, it is fine to stand by while the work continues.

rules.quote: turn after a brief status update.
rules.rule: If at least one agent is in flight, end the turn after a brief status update.

rules.quote: NO → must dispatch.
rules.rule: If no agent is in flight, dispatch an agent rather than stopping.

rules.quote: → dispatch an agent for it.
rules.rule: If a clear next task exists (queued in TaskList, mentioned in the user's prior message, or implied by the last commit), dispatch an agent for it.

rules.quote: pick one and go. Don't ask.
rules.rule: If multiple candidate next tasks exist, pick one and proceed without asking the user.

rules.quote: Schedule a self-wakeup 15 minutes (900 seconds) out via
rules.rule: When you would benefit from user input but must proceed, schedule a self-wakeup 15 minutes (900 seconds) out via ScheduleWakeup.

rules.quote: Send the user a brief text + voice describing what I'm
rules.rule: When you would benefit from user input, send the user a brief text and voice message describing the question and noting the 15-minute fallback is set.

rules.quote: Read the docs/plans/ tree + `MEMORY.md` + the current
rules.rule: When all planned work is done, read the docs/plans/ tree, MEMORY.md, and the current SESSION_STATE.

rules.quote: Pick something unimplemented. Dispatch it.
rules.rule: When all planned work is done, pick an unimplemented item from the docs and dispatch an agent for it.

rules.quote: pick one and dispatch.
rules.rule: Instead of asking what to do next, pick one task and dispatch it.

rules.quote: mention B in the commit message as a deferred alternative.
rules.rule: When choosing between alternatives A and B, ship A and mention B in the commit message as a deferred alternative instead of asking.

rules.quote: dispatch first
rules.rule: Instead of waiting for the user to say go, dispatch first and then tell the user what was done and to flag it if the direction is wrong.

rules.quote: schedule wakeup + dispatch a reasonable next thing.
rules.rule: When no agent is working and you would otherwise stand by for the user's call, schedule a wakeup and dispatch a reasonable next thing.

rules.quote: End the turn quietly.
rules.rule: When multiple agents are in flight on tightly-coupled files, do not open a third stream; end the turn quietly.

rules.quote: Tests running in CI — wait for the result.
rules.rule: While tests are running in CI, wait for the result.

rules.quote: wait, but schedule the wakeup as a safety net.
rules.rule: When a task is explicitly blocked on external state, wait, but schedule a wakeup as a safety net.

rules.quote: Don't cut corners on verification just
rules.rule: Do not skip verification inside dispatched work just because you are picking tasks quickly.

rules.quote: the text carries the same content + the wakeup time.
rules.rule: When scheduling a wakeup and texting the user, the text should carry the same content as the voice message plus the wakeup time.

rules.quote: Category filter chips, tab strips for filter navigation, and similar small-discrete-navigation surfaces must NEVER horizontally scroll.
rules.rule: Never horizontally scroll category filter chips, filter tab strips, or similar small discrete navigation surfaces.

rules.quote: **Wrap to multiple rows.** A 4-chip strip that doesn't fit on one row becomes 2 rows of 2. Flex-wrap is your friend.
rules.rule: When category chips don't fit on one row, wrap them onto multiple rows instead of scrolling.

rules.quote: **Use smaller chips or icons** if real estate is tight.
rules.rule: When space is tight for category chips, use smaller chips or icons.

rules.quote: switch to a single icon-only kebab or "More…" dropdown. But that's a last resort — wrap rows are almost always enough.
rules.rule: Only when category chips cannot fit even in two wrapped rows at very narrow widths (under about 140px), use a single icon-only kebab or "More…" dropdown as a last resort.

rules.quote: **Where `<ScrollRow>` IS appropriate (it's not banned, just don't put it here):**
rules.rule: Use ScrollRow for long content lists, tag clouds where overflow into a "more" is acceptable, and horizontal carousels of large preview cards, but not for navigation chip strips.

rules.quote: Are these chips a primary navigation surface (filters, tabs, modes)? → NO ScrollRow. Wrap rows.
rules.rule: Before putting chips in ScrollRow, if they are a primary navigation surface (filters, tabs, modes), do not use ScrollRow and wrap rows instead.

rules.quote: Is the user expected to discover all options at a glance? → NO ScrollRow.
rules.rule: Do not use ScrollRow for chip strips where the user is expected to discover all options at a glance.

rules.quote: Is the option count fixed and small (≤8)? → NO ScrollRow.
rules.rule: Do not use ScrollRow for chip strips with a fixed, small option count (8 or fewer).

rules.quote: Is it a search-results-style overflow where seeing "20 more" makes sense to scroll? → ScrollRow is OK.
rules.rule: ScrollRow is acceptable for search-results-style overflow where scrolling to see additional items makes sense.

rules.quote: Hard rule: no worktrees on this project.
rules.rule: Never use git worktrees on this project.

rules.quote: Never pass `isolation: "worktree"` to the Agent tool.
rules.rule: Never pass isolation: "worktree" to the Agent tool; run agents in the main checkout instead.

rules.quote: For overlapping work, serialize.
rules.rule: For overlapping work, serialize agent dispatches rather than running them in parallel.

rules.quote: Don't dispatch 6 agents in parallel if two of them touch the same file
rules.rule: Do not dispatch agents in parallel when two of them touch the same file.

rules.quote: Run them one at a time; each agent commits + pushes before the next begins.
rules.rule: Run overlapping agents one at a time, with each agent committing and pushing before the next begins.

rules.quote: For non-overlapping work, parallel is still fine
rules.rule: For non-overlapping work, parallel agent dispatch is allowed.

rules.quote: they must all operate against the same main checkout.
rules.rule: Parallel agents working on non-overlapping files must all operate against the same main checkout.

rules.quote: don't run `git worktree remove --force` unsupervised
rules.rule: Do not run git worktree remove --force unsupervised to clean up leftover worktrees; leave that to the user.

rules.quote: orchestrator pre-stages the shared edits in a single commit FIRST, then dispatches per-panel agents that only touch their own panel file.
rules.rule: When panels share a file, the orchestrator must first stage the shared edits in a single commit before dispatching per-panel agents that touch only their own panel file.

rules.quote: For "fix" waves where each agent edits ONE panel file: serialize them.
rules.rule: For fix waves where each agent edits one panel file, serialize the agents rather than running them in parallel.

rules.quote: never dispatch next batch until previous merged + pushed cleanly.
rules.rule: Do not dispatch the next batch until the previous batch is merged and pushed cleanly.

rules.quote: Every page must register 3-5 predefined layouts in `apps/editor/src/state/predefinedLayouts.ts` keyed by page id.
rules.rule: When building a page, register 3-5 predefined layouts for it in `apps/editor/src/state/predefinedLayouts.ts`, keyed by page id.

rules.quote: Each layout has an id, a human label, a `SerializedDockview` JSON snapshot, and an optional description.
rules.rule: Give each predefined layout an id, a human-readable label, a `SerializedDockview` JSON snapshot, and optionally a description.

rules.quote: also make sure any shared dock panels exist in the panel modal.
rules.rule: Make sure every shared dock panel is available in the panel modal.

rules.quote: every page should expose additional opt-in panels via the Docks modal.
rules.rule: Expose page-specific opt-in dock panels on every page via the Docks modal, including panels that are not in the default layout.

rules.quote: Pick 2-4 sensible ones and build stubs in Phase 1
rules.rule: Pick 2-4 sensible opt-in panels for each page and build stubs for them in Phase 1.

rules.quote: bodies in a later wave.
rules.rule: Implement the bodies of opt-in panel stubs in a later wave, not in Phase 1.

rules.quote: These panels must be registered in EVERY page's PANELS array.
rules.rule: Register every shared dock panel in every page's PANELS array.

rules.quote: Factor a `SHARED_PANELS` constant in `apps/editor/src/views/sharedPanels.ts`
rules.rule: Define a `SHARED_PANELS` constant in `apps/editor/src/views/sharedPanels.ts`.

rules.quote: that each page imports and spreads into its own PANELS array.
rules.rule: Have each page import `SHARED_PANELS` and spread it into its own PANELS array.

rules.quote: Persistence keys for page-scoped panels use the page id prefix (`cardboard.<page>.notes.text`).
rules.rule: Prefix persistence keys for page-scoped panels with the page id, e.g. `cardboard.<page>.notes.text`.

rules.quote: Every panel-body agent must design for that from the start.
rules.rule: Every panel-body agent must design for unpredictable panel sizes and shapes from the start.

rules.quote: no native horizontal scrollbar
rules.rule: Never expose a native horizontal scrollbar on panels.

rules.quote: Use the hover-area pattern from `apps/editor/src/components/ui/TabStrip.tsx` (`scrollable={true}` mode)
rules.rule: Use the hover-area pattern from apps/editor/src/components/ui/TabStrip.tsx (scrollable={true} mode) for horizontal overflow.

rules.quote: Edge fades only appear when the content actually overflows the panel width
rules.rule: Show edge fades only when the content actually overflows the panel width, and hide them when content fits.

rules.quote: Hovering an edge fade triggers continuous auto-scroll in that direction.
rules.rule: Make hovering an edge fade trigger continuous auto-scroll in that direction.

rules.quote: Clicking a fade jumps to the extreme.
rules.rule: Make clicking an edge fade jump to the extreme of the content in that direction.

rules.quote: When content fits, no fades, no chrome.
rules.rule: When content fits the panel, show no edge fades or scroll chrome.

rules.quote: each row gets its own `<ScrollRow>` container; don't share a parent overflow.
rules.rule: Give each row of items its own ScrollRow container and do not share a parent overflow between rows.

rules.quote: every tile / button must have a `min-w-*` that prevents collapse below something useful
rules.rule: Give every tile or button a min-w-* minimum width that prevents it from collapsing below a useful size.

rules.quote: Responsive logic is per-panel, not universal.
rules.rule: Design responsive logic per panel to fit that panel's contents, not as one universal reflow pattern.

rules.quote: every panel should *think about* wide / tall / square dock shapes when its body is built.
rules.rule: Make every panel consider wide, tall, and square dock shapes when its body is built.

rules.quote: Per-panel agent briefs must call out
rules.rule: Per-panel agent briefs must call out the aspect ratios the panel might see and the agent's specific strategy for each.

rules.quote: For button-or-icon grids specifically
rules.rule: For button-or-icon grids, use auto-fit with minmax reflow so the grid moves from vertical stack to horizontal row as the panel widens.

rules.quote: Document the choice in the panel's docstring.
rules.rule: Document the chosen layout or overflow approach in the panel's docstring when content is not a button or icon grid.

rules.quote: native vertical scroll for long lists
rules.rule: Use native vertical scroll for long lists.

rules.quote: native scrollbars are acceptable
rules.rule: Native vertical scrollbars are acceptable for vertical overflow.

rules.quote: responsive design is a HEAVY focus; panel widths/heights are unpredictable. Use the TabStrip `scrollable` pattern from `apps/editor/src/components/ui/TabStrip.tsx` as the overflow affordance — never expose native scrollbars.
rules.rule: Every panel-body agent brief must state that responsive design is a heavy focus and that the TabStrip scrollable pattern from apps/editor/src/components/ui/TabStrip.tsx is the overflow affordance, never exposing native scrollbars.

rules.quote: extract the pattern into a shared `<ScrollArea>` primitive under `apps/editor/src/components/ui/` rather than re-implement it inline.
rules.rule: When the first panel needs vertical-scroll behavior, extract the pattern into a shared ScrollArea primitive under apps/editor/src/components/ui/ instead of re-implementing it inline.

rules.quote: Future panels import that primitive.
rules.rule: Future panels must import the shared ScrollArea primitive rather than re-implementing scroll behavior.

rules.quote: Content density must adapt — short labels on narrow widths, full labels on wide.
rules.rule: Make content density adapt to panel width, using short labels on narrow widths and full labels on wide widths.

rules.quote: Use `@container` queries or `ResizeObserver` where Tailwind responsive breakpoints (window-width based) won't help
rules.rule: Use @container queries or ResizeObserver instead of window-width Tailwind breakpoints for panel-responsive layout.

rules.quote: Tile/button grids should use `grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fit,minmax(40px,1fr))]` or similar so the layout reflows naturally.
rules.rule: Use an auto-fit minmax grid such as grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fit,minmax(40px,1fr))] for tile or button grids so the layout reflows naturally.

rules.quote: Avoid fixed-column-count grids unless the spec explicitly requires it
rules.rule: Avoid fixed-column-count grids unless the spec explicitly requires one.

rules.quote: send all the `Agent` tool calls in a **single assistant message** so they run concurrently
rules.rule: When delegating multiple independent pieces of work to Agent subagents, send all the Agent tool calls in a single assistant message so they run concurrently.

rules.quote: Don't dispatch one, wait for it, then dispatch the next when the second didn't need the first's output.
rules.rule: Do not dispatch an Agent subagent, wait for it to finish, and only then dispatch the next one when the next one does not need the first one's output.

rules.quote: If no → bundle them all into one message.
rules.rule: If later Agent subagents need no output from earlier ones, bundle them all into one message.

rules.quote: If yes → only serialise the dependent ones; everything else still parallelises.
rules.rule: If a later Agent subagent needs output from an earlier one, serialise only the dependent agents and still parallelise all the others.

rules.quote: multiple independent implementation agents can fan out from one Explore result
rules.rule: Multiple independent implementation agents may be dispatched in parallel after a single Explore agent's result is returned.

rules.quote: always pass a `filename:` value that begins with `screenshots/`
rules.rule: When calling `mcp__playwright__browser_take_screenshot`, always pass a `filename` value that begins with `screenshots/`.

rules.quote: Every `browser_take_screenshot` call must set `filename` to `screenshots/<descriptive-name>.png`.
rules.rule: Every `browser_take_screenshot` call must set `filename` to `screenshots/<descriptive-name>.png`.

rules.quote: Never leave PNGs in repo root.
rules.rule: Never leave Playwright screenshot PNG files in the repository root.

rules.quote: always be explicit.
rules.rule: Always explicitly specify the screenshot filename rather than relying on the default output location (cwd or `.playwright-mcp/`).

rules.quote: All cross-panel state (selection, active tool, brush, layers, history, etc.) MUST work perfectly even when a panel is popped out into its own browser window.
rules.rule: Make all cross-panel state (selection, active tool, brush, layers, history, etc.) work correctly when a panel is popped out into its own browser window.

rules.quote: design the wiring layer for cross-window communication from day one.
rules.rule: Design the wiring layer for cross-window communication from the start of the project.

rules.quote: Zustand stores wrap with `zustand/middleware/persist`, writing to localStorage under a scoped key.
rules.rule: Wrap state that should survive reloads in a Zustand store using `zustand/middleware/persist`, writing to localStorage under a scoped key.

rules.quote: A `useEffect` in each store's hook attaches a `window.addEventListener("storage", ...)` listener.
rules.rule: Attach a `window.addEventListener("storage", ...)` listener in a `useEffect` in each persisted store's hook.

rules.quote: When the storage event fires (from another window writing to the same key), it re-hydrates the store from the new value.
rules.rule: When a storage event fires from another window writing to the same key, re-hydrate the store from the new value.

rules.quote: Use the `BroadcastChannel` API
rules.rule: Use the `BroadcastChannel` API to propagate ephemeral state between windows.

rules.quote: Pair with a Zustand store that listens + writes to local state on receipt.
rules.rule: Pair each BroadcastChannel with a Zustand store that listens on the channel and writes received data to local state.

rules.quote: **One store per concern**
rules.rule: Use one Zustand store per concern.

rules.quote: Each persists its relevant slice + subscribes to cross-window sync.
rules.rule: Have each store persist its relevant slice and subscribe to cross-window sync.

rules.quote: **Avoid storing references**
rules.rule: Avoid storing references in stores.

rules.quote: only serializable data (numbers, strings, plain objects, arrays)
rules.rule: Store only serializable data (numbers, strings, plain objects, arrays) in stores.

rules.quote: throttle / debounce ephemeral broadcasts to ~30Hz, or only emit on cell-grid boundary crossings.
rules.rule: Throttle or debounce ephemeral broadcasts to ~30Hz, or emit them only on cell-grid boundary crossings.

rules.quote: When testing Wave 3 wiring, ALWAYS test the popout path:
rules.rule: When testing Wave 3 wiring, always test the popout path.

rules.quote: Make a state change in the popout.
rules.rule: When testing the popout path, make a state change in the popout window.

rules.quote: Verify the change is reflected in the orchestrator window.
rules.rule: When testing the popout path, verify the change is reflected in the orchestrator window.

rules.quote: Reverse direction.
rules.rule: When testing the popout path, repeat the state change test in the reverse direction.

rules.quote: Reload both windows — verify state persists where it should.
rules.rule: When testing the popout path, reload both windows and verify state persists where it should.

rules.quote: Build new stores on top of this utility.
rules.rule: Build new stores on top of the cross-window sync utility module.

rules.quote: Do NOT build Wave 3 stores without the cross-window sync layer
rules.rule: Do NOT build Wave 3 stores without the cross-window sync layer.

rules.quote: Apply to every interactive element where context-on-hover is useful.
rules.rule: Use the progressive tooltip as the hover affordance for every interactive element where context-on-hover is useful.

rules.quote: 2 seconds hover** → tooltip appears with the element's **short name / label**
rules.rule: Show a tooltip with the element's short name or label after a 2-second hover.

rules.quote: 5 seconds hover** → tooltip swaps to show the **short name AND a fuller description**
rules.rule: After a 5-second hover, swap the tooltip to show both the short name and a fuller description.

rules.quote: Hover-away cancels both pending stages and hides the tooltip immediately.
rules.rule: When the cursor leaves the element, cancel any pending tooltip stages and hide the tooltip immediately.

rules.quote: new interactive content should default to the staged pattern.
rules.rule: Default new interactive content to the staged two-stage tooltip pattern rather than a single-content tooltip.

rules.quote: The single-`content` Tooltip mode is still supported and used for trivial labels (e.g. a close button)
rules.rule: Use the single-content Tooltip mode only for trivial labels, such as a close button.

rules.quote: every interactive control's label and description should live on its fixture / config / manifest entry so the tooltip wraps it consistently.
rules.rule: Store every interactive control's label and description on its fixture, config, or manifest entry so its tooltip is wrapped consistently.

rules.quote: every panel-build dispatch must include "wrap interactive controls in `<Tooltip stages={...}>` per [[feedback-progressive-tooltips]]".
rules.rule: When dispatching a panel-build agent brief, include the instruction to wrap interactive controls in `<Tooltip stages={...}>` per the progressive-tooltips standard.

rules.quote: The 2s/5s timing is project-wide and shouldn't be tuned per-panel.
rules.rule: Do not tune the 2s and 5s tooltip delays per panel; keep them project-wide.

rules.quote: Every response that uses voice MUST also include text that carries the same substantive content.
rules.rule: Whenever a response uses voice synthesis, also include text that carries the same substantive content.

rules.quote: Voice is a *companion* to text, not a substitute for it.
rules.rule: Do not use voice as a substitute for text; voice must accompany text, never replace it.

rules.quote: even if the voice has fully narrated the milestone, end with a 1-2 line text summary.
rules.rule: Even when voice has already narrated a milestone, end the turn with a 1-2 line text summary.

rules.quote: Don't end on tool calls or pure voice.
rules.rule: Do not end a turn on tool calls or on voice alone; end with text.

rules.quote: Always TTS the question content when calling AskUserQuestion.
rules.rule: When calling AskUserQuestion, also speak the question content aloud via TTS.

rules.quote: Whenever calling `AskUserQuestion`, ALSO call `mcp__voice__synthesize` in the same turn with the question content.
rules.rule: Whenever calling AskUserQuestion, also call mcp__voice__synthesize in the same turn with the question content.

rules.quote: Don't rely on the visual UI alone
rules.rule: Do not rely solely on the visual UI to present questions; always provide the audio channel as well.

rules.quote: A short phrase indicating a question is being asked.
rules.rule: The voice TTS call paired with AskUserQuestion should include a short phrase indicating a question is being asked.

rules.quote: The substance of the question (not just "I'm asking something").
rules.rule: The voice TTS call paired with AskUserQuestion should include the substance of the question, not merely a generic statement that a question is being asked.

rules.quote: Optionally, the recommended option.
rules.rule: The voice TTS call paired with AskUserQuestion may include the recommended option.

rules.quote: **Always pair `AskUserQuestion` with a voice TTS call**
rules.rule: Always pair AskUserQuestion with a voice TTS call.

rules.quote: The voice carries content; the AskUserQuestion is the formal capture.
rules.rule: The voice TTS content carries the substantive question content, while AskUserQuestion serves as the formal capture of the question.

rules.quote:
verify it via
`grep`, `Read`, or `git log` in the same turn
rules.rule: Before stating a factual claim about project state, verify it via grep, Read, or git log in the same turn.

rules.quote: say so explicitly
rules.rule: If a factual claim about project state cannot be verified cheaply, say explicitly that it is unverified (e.g., "I'd need to check" or "my guess is X but I haven't verified").

rules.quote: Before sending any response, re-read the draft with the lens
rules.rule: Before sending any response, re-read the draft and check every factual claim in it by asking how to prove it is true.

rules.quote: verify it BEFORE sending; rewrite if the claim turns out wrong.
rules.rule: If a factual claim in a draft can be verified cheaply (grep, Read, git, ls, typecheck), verify it before sending and rewrite it if it turns out wrong.

rules.quote: → hedge the claim explicitly
rules.rule: If a factual claim in a draft is expensive to verify, hedge it explicitly in the response (e.g., "I think X but haven't verified") or omit it.

rules.quote: no verification needed; ship as-is.
rules.rule: Do not verify subjective recommendations or analysis; ship them as-is.

rules.quote: run `git log --reverse --format='%ad %s' --date=short | head -3`
rules.rule: Before stating a duration (e.g., "for weeks", "since Phase 2"), check the dates with git log, such as git log --reverse --format='%ad %s' --date=short | head -3, or check the specific file's git log.

rules.quote: grep + `wc -l` the actual matches.
rules.rule: Before stating a count (e.g., "24 panels"), grep and wc -l the actual matches.

rules.quote: grep first.
rules.rule: Before quoting a file path or function/identifier name, grep for it first.

rules.quote: Never quote a path or identifier from memory of "what I think the codebase looks like."
rules.rule: Never quote a file path or identifier from memory of what you think the codebase looks like.

rules.quote: verify the hash exists, run the check, or hedge.
rules.rule: Before stating a commit hash or status claim (e.g., "tests pass", "tsc clean"), verify the hash exists, run the check, or hedge the claim.

rules.quote: the next tool call is a verification
rules.rule: When caught making a wrong factual claim, make the next tool call a verification (grep, Read, or git), not a defensive explanation.

rules.quote: *"The reason is..."* without verifying first.
rules.rule: Do not give an explanation such as "The reason is..." for a wrong claim without verifying it first.

rules.quote: say *"a few days"* rather than risking a wrong number.
rules.rule: In voice (TTS) responses, use approximate wording (e.g., "a few days") instead of a specific number you have not verified.

rules.quote: verify BEFORE synthesizing.
rules.rule: In voice (TTS) responses, verify any fact that the substantive content depends on before synthesizing the audio.

rules.quote: **voice synthesis must contain that content**
rules.rule: When a turn produces findings, a status report, a list of changes, or another meaningful result, the voice synthesis must contain that content, not a short placeholder intro like "let me check" or "on it."

rules.quote: If a turn has a single meaningful response, voice that response
rules.rule: When a turn has a single meaningful response, voice that response in the voice synthesis.

rules.quote: the findings is what gets voiced
rules.rule: When a turn has both an intro action and a findings report, voice the findings.

rules.quote: either skip the intro or roll it into the same voice call
rules.rule: When a turn has both an intro action and a findings report, you may skip the intro or combine it into the same voice call as the findings.

rules.quote: the second voice carries the substantive content.
rules.rule: If you must voice more than once in a turn, make the second voice carry the substantive content.

rules.quote: Don't truncate.
rules.rule: Do not truncate the spoken summary.

rules.quote: The spoken summary should match the depth of the text response.
rules.rule: Make the spoken summary match the depth of the text response.

rules.quote: the voice mentions the main ones
rules.rule: When the text response has many points, have the spoken summary mention the main ones rather than reducing it to a vague summary such as "everything's fine."

rules.quote: One-line confirmations ("audio delivered", "merged + pushed") are fine when they ARE the substantive content
rules.rule: A one-line confirmation is acceptable as the voice content when it is the substantive content of the turn.

rules.quote: When a voice response is long enough that a single synthesis would run past ~20 seconds, split it into multiple synthesize → pipe pairs and run them in sequence within the same turn.
rules.rule: When a voice response would take more than about 20 seconds to synthesize as one call, split it into multiple synthesize→pipe pairs and run them in sequence within the same turn.

rules.quote: Don't try to cram a paragraph-plus into one call.
rules.rule: Do not cram a paragraph-plus of voice content into a single synthesize call.

rules.quote: synthesize text under ~55 words / ~350 chars per call.
rules.rule: Keep the text for each voice synthesize call under about 55 words or 350 characters.

rules.quote: split at natural sentence boundaries.
rules.rule: When splitting a long voice response into chunks, split at natural sentence boundaries.

rules.quote: never split mid-sentence.
rules.rule: Never split a voice response chunk mid-sentence.

rules.quote: Each chunk is a complete sentence (or two short sentences) that stands on its own
rules.rule: Make each voice chunk a complete sentence (or two short sentences) that stands on its own.

rules.quote: strictly serial, never parallel:
rules.rule: Run voice synthesize→pipe pairs strictly serially, never in parallel.

rules.quote: NEVER batch multiple `synthesize` calls in a single parallel tool-use block.
rules.rule: Never batch multiple synthesize calls in a single parallel tool-use block.

rules.quote: the next pair only starts after the previous pipe returns.
rules.rule: Start the next synthesize→pipe pair only after the previous pipe call has returned.

rules.quote: All synth+pipe pairs run BEFORE other tool calls per `[[feedback-voice-mcp-playback]]`.
rules.rule: Run all voice synth+pipe pairs before any other tool calls in the turn.

rules.quote: every chunk should carry real findings, not filler.
rules.rule: Make every voice chunk carry real substance rather than filler.

rules.quote: Don't pad to hit the 20s target; cut content if a chunk falls short of substance.
rules.rule: Do not pad voice chunks to reach the 20-second target; cut content from a chunk that lacks substance instead.

rules.quote: When the response is genuinely short (one sentence), one chunk is correct — don't artificially split.
rules.rule: When a voice response is genuinely short, use a single chunk and do not artificially split it.

rules.quote: For every response, lead with a `mcp__voice__synthesize` call
rules.rule: For every response, begin the turn with a mcp__voice__synthesize call before anything else.

rules.quote: omit `play_local`, pipe the returned URL through the response's "Recommended playback" command in a background Bash
rules.rule: When calling mcp__voice__synthesize, omit the play_local parameter and pipe the returned URL through the response's "Recommended playback" command in a background Bash.

rules.quote: Keep the spoken text to **one paragraph or less**
rules.rule: Keep the spoken text of each voice synthesis call to one paragraph or less.

rules.quote: a concise summary of what's about to happen or what just finished
rules.rule: Make the spoken text a concise summary of what is about to happen or what just finished, not the full detailed response.

rules.quote: Then write the full detailed text response below it.
rules.rule: After the voice call, write the full detailed text response below it.

rules.quote: never the long detailed response itself
rules.rule: Never use the long detailed response itself as the spoken text in a voice synthesis call.

rules.quote: Voice synthesize and the playback Bash are the FIRST TWO tool calls of every turn, in that order, BEFORE any other work.
rules.rule: At the start of every turn, make the voice synthesize tool call first and the playback Bash command second, before any other work.

rules.quote: **First tool call**: `mcp__voice__synthesize` (omit `play_local`).
rules.rule: Make `mcp__voice__synthesize` the first tool call of each turn, omitting the `play_local` parameter.

rules.quote: **WITHOUT `run_in_background`** so playback runs in the FOREGROUND and blocks until the audio finishes.
rules.rule: Run the recommended playback Bash command without `run_in_background` so playback runs in the foreground and blocks until the audio finishes.

rules.quote: **THEN, and only then**: any other tool calls.
rules.rule: Make any other tool calls only after the synthesize and playback calls have been made.

rules.quote: Nothing else goes between them.
rules.rule: Do not place any other tool call between the synthesize call and the playback Bash call.

rules.quote: Do NOT parallel-batch synthesize with other tool calls.
rules.rule: Do not batch the synthesize call in parallel with other tool calls.

rules.quote: Multiple voices in one turn: each one is synth → pipe foreground → next work, in series.
rules.rule: When producing multiple voice responses in one turn, run each as synthesize then foreground playback then next work, in series.

rules.quote: Pipe the substantive voice immediately even if late.
rules.rule: If the turn's voice output was missed or only an intro was voiced, pipe the substantive voice immediately even if it is late.

rules.quote: Never dispatch a new wave of agents until the previous wave's work is fully merged into main
rules.rule: Never dispatch a new batch of parallel worktree agents until the previous batch's work is fully merged into main.

rules.quote: Before dispatching ANY new batch of parallel worktree agents, the previous batch MUST be in this state:
rules.rule: Before dispatching any new batch of parallel worktree agents, verify the previous batch is fully merged, conflict-free, typechecked, pushed, and committed.

rules.quote: Every commit from the previous batch cherry-picked into `main`
rules.rule: Cherry-pick every commit from the previous batch into main (or merge it equivalently) before dispatching the next batch.

rules.quote: All conflicts resolved
rules.rule: Resolve all cherry-pick or merge conflicts before dispatching the next batch.

rules.quote: no abort/skip cherry-picks left dangling
rules.rule: Do not leave cherry-picks dangling in an aborted or skipped state before dispatching the next batch.

rules.quote: `bun run typecheck` from `apps/editor/` exits 0
rules.rule: Run `bun run typecheck` from `apps/editor/` on the current main HEAD and confirm it exits 0 before dispatching the next batch.

rules.quote: `git push origin main` succeeded
rules.rule: Run `git push origin main` and confirm it succeeds before dispatching the next batch.

rules.quote: `git status` is clean
rules.rule: Confirm `git status` is clean (no uncommitted modifications or untracked files that should be tracked) before dispatching the next batch.

rules.quote: Only THEN dispatch the next wave.
rules.rule: Dispatch the next batch of agents only after all pre-dispatch conditions are met.

rules.quote: Prefer `git cherry-pick <sha>` over `git merge` for each agent's branch
rules.rule: Prefer `git cherry-pick <sha>` over `git merge` when integrating each agent's branch.

rules.quote: Always check `git log --oneline -5` to confirm what's actually on main before cherry-picking.
rules.rule: Always check `git log --oneline -5` to confirm what is on main before cherry-picking.

rules.quote: If cherry-pick stalls with "nothing to commit" and is non-empty diff, investigate before continuing
rules.rule: If a cherry-pick stalls with "nothing to commit" despite a non-empty diff, investigate before continuing.

rules.quote: `cd` back to the project root and retry
rules.rule: When a cherry-pick stalls because the working directory shifted into a worktree, cd back to the project root and retry.

rules.quote: pre-stage the shared changes yourself in a single commit BEFORE dispatching the dependent agents
rules.rule: For shared files likely to conflict across agents, pre-stage the shared changes yourself in a single commit before dispatching the dependent agents.

rules.quote: Never skip the gate "because the agents need to start now."
rules.rule: Never skip the pre-dispatch gate because agents need to start now.

rules.quote: If any check fails, FIX before dispatching.
rules.rule: If any pre-dispatch check fails, fix it before dispatching agents.

rules.quote: Don't dispatch 3.3 work until the DnD plan doc + payload contract + DropZone primitive + useAssetStore + useDragStore are at least specified, ideally also scaffolded.
rules.rule: Do not dispatch Wave 3.3 panel migration work until the DnD plan doc, payload contract, DropZone primitive, useAssetStore, and useDragStore are at least specified.

rules.quote: When migrating a panel in Wave 3.3, write it as a drag source AND/OR drop target depending on its role — see the integration matrix in the plan doc.
rules.rule: When migrating a panel in Wave 3.3, write it as a drag source and/or drop target depending on its role, following the integration matrix in the plan doc.

rules.quote: Each draggable kind gets its own MIME type prefix (`application/x-cardboard-*`) so drop zones can filter by `accepts`.
rules.rule: Give each draggable kind its own MIME type with the prefix `application/x-cardboard-*` so drop zones can filter by `accepts`.

rules.quote: Everything else — including our own editor — is a pack on top
rules.rule: Ship only the shell in Cardboard, and implement everything else, including the editor itself, as a pack on top of the shell.

rules.quote: Toolbars, layouts, the home screen, the project
rules.rule: Do not put toolbars, layouts, the home screen, the project picker, or scene tabs in the shell; place them in the core editor pack.

rules.quote: Every dock panel — ToolPalette, Brush, TilePresets, Layers,
rules.rule: Place every dock panel (such as ToolPalette, Brush, TilePresets, Layers) in the core editor pack, not in the shell.

rules.quote: Anything game-domain-specific — fixtures, hardcoded layer
rules.rule: Keep game-domain-specific code (fixtures, hardcoded layer taxonomies, hardcoded tile preset categories) out of the shell; put it in the core editor pack or a game-domain pack chained after it.

rules.quote: No "special editor APIs."
rules.rule: Do not create special APIs that only the editor can use.

rules.quote: No hidden surfaces.
rules.rule: Do not create hidden surfaces that only the editor can access.

rules.quote: Same docs, same examples, same imports.
rules.rule: Give the editor the same docs, examples, and imports that third-party pack authors use.

rules.quote: in the shell or as a published primitive.
rules.rule: When a third party could reasonably need a capability, put it in the shell or expose it as a published primitive.

rules.quote: If no — it goes in the
rules.rule: When a third party would not reasonably need a capability, put it in the core editor pack.

rules.quote: The shell should expose what we use.
rules.rule: If the editor uses a different mechanism than a third party would, expose that mechanism through the shell so third parties can use it too.

rules.quote: Find a way to make it a normal primitive.
rules.rule: If a feature needs a hook only the editor has access to, redesign it as a normal primitive available to all packs.

rules.quote: fix the API before shipping it.
rules.rule: If shipping an API would embarrass us in front of a community-pack author, fix the API before shipping it.

rules.quote: we extend the shell — and EVERYONE benefits
rules.rule: When the editor needs something the shell does not expose, extend the shell instead of adding a private hook.

rules.quote: `apps/editor/` shrinks to the shell.
rules.rule: Reduce apps/editor/ so that it contains only the shell.

rules.quote: `packages/core-editor-pack/` (new workspace) holds everything
rules.rule: Move the editor views, panels, and page chrome from apps/editor/ into the packages/core-editor-pack/ workspace.

rules.quote: those writes must land in IDB
rules.rule: When the user paints, edits scripts, or tweaks an entity, the resulting write must land in IDB.

rules.quote: LS-backed Zustand stores can hold UI state (active tool, brush size) but NOT asset content.
rules.rule: Do not store asset content in LocalStorage-backed Zustand stores; they may hold only UI state.

rules.quote: Don't confuse "synced Zustand store" with "asset storage"
rules.rule: Do not treat a synced Zustand store as asset storage; they are different layers.

rules.quote: must be a **reactive view over IDB**, NOT a `createSyncedStore`
rules.rule: Any planned useAssetStore must be a reactive view over IDB, not a createSyncedStore.

rules.quote: default to "IDB-backed with BroadcastChannel for cross-window invalidation," not "LS-backed Zustand."
rules.rule: When designing a new asset, script, or scene-content store, default to an IDB-backed store with BroadcastChannel cross-window invalidation, not an LS-backed Zustand store.

rules.quote: the payload references an IDB record by id/path
rules.rule: When wiring DnD payloads, make the payload reference an IDB record by id or path.

rules.quote: the drop handler reads from IDB to resolve
rules.rule: When handling a DnD drop, read the referenced record from IDB to resolve it.

rules.quote: check whether its data lives in IDB
rules.rule: When migrating a Wave-3.3 panel that touches content, check whether its data lives in IDB.

rules.quote: route reads/writes through `EditorProjectStore`
rules.rule: When a content panel reads or writes project data, route those reads and writes through EditorProjectStore.

rules.quote: not through a new LS store
rules.rule: Do not route content reads or writes through a new LocalStorage store.

rules.quote: Engine-side reads (playtest, export) MUST work without the editor running
rules.rule: Ensure engine-side reads for playtest and export work without the editor running.

rules.quote: the IDB contract is owned by the engine package
rules.rule: Treat the IDB contract as owned by the engine package.

rules.quote: the editor's view layer adapts to it
rules.rule: Make the editor's view layer adapt to the engine-owned IDB contract.

rules.quote: Don't render cubes/spheres for entities.
rules.rule: Do not render cubes or spheres for entities; represent entities as billboard sprites.

rules.quote: There are NO 3D meshes for entities.
rules.rule: Do not use 3D meshes for entities.

rules.quote: EntityPreviewPanel and similar previews must show sprites, not cubes/spheres.
rules.rule: Entity preview panels and similar previews must show sprites, not cubes or spheres.

rules.quote: Render a single textured quad that billboards toward the camera.
rules.rule: For entity previews, render a single textured quad that billboards toward the camera.

rules.quote: Even the placeholder should be a flat quad
rules.rule: Make entity placeholder geometry a flat quad, not a 3D shape.

rules.quote: The MapCanvas placeholder geometry of "walls" is fine
rules.rule: Placeholder 3D geometry for walls in MapCanvas is allowed.

rules.quote: that's allowed because it's a 3D PREVIEW of how the raycaster RESULT looks
rules.rule: The 3D PreviewPanel on the Scene page may show a perspective 3D view of the raycaster result.

rules.quote: entity-specific previews (in the Prefabs page) should show the sprite asset, not a 3D mesh.
rules.rule: Entity-specific previews on the Prefabs page should show the sprite asset, not a 3D mesh.

rules.quote: default to sprite-thinking unless explicitly working on the 3D Scene Preview.
rules.rule: When building entity-rendering surfaces, default to sprite-based rendering unless explicitly working on the 3D Scene Preview.

rules.quote: Replace with a billboard sprite
rules.rule: Replace the cube/sphere rendering in EntityPreviewPanel with a billboard sprite.

rules.quote: with the plane's rotation locked to face the camera via `mesh.quaternion.copy(camera.quaternion)` in the render loop
rules.rule: Lock the billboard plane's rotation to face the camera by copying the camera quaternion in the render loop.

rules.quote: Keep the orbit camera so the user can verify the billboard always faces them.
rules.rule: Keep the orbit camera in EntityPreviewPanel so the user can verify the billboard faces them.

rules.quote: Design the seams in the current sync.ts transport NOW even if implementation lands later
rules.rule: When working on the sync.ts transport, design its seams now, even if the network transport is implemented later.

rules.quote: design D4–D7 of the DnD plan so PeerJS plugs in later without a retrofit
rules.rule: Design D4–D7 of the DnD plan so a PeerJS transport can be plugged in later without retrofitting.

rules.quote: Treat that as a transport INTERFACE.
rules.rule: Treat createSyncedStore's transport as an interface that a future PeerJS transport can satisfy.

rules.quote: don't write code that pokes `localStorage` directly
rules.rule: Don't write code that accesses localStorage directly.

rules.quote: or assumes `storage` event semantics
rules.rule: Don't write code that assumes `storage` event semantics.

rules.quote: Go through `createSyncedStore`'s API.
rules.rule: Go through createSyncedStore's API when reading or writing synced store state.

rules.quote: If it's missing, extend the API rather than bypassing it.
rules.rule: If createSyncedStore's API lacks needed functionality, extend the API rather than bypassing it.

rules.quote: all `set(...)` calls that originate from a remote peer should be flagged
rules.rule: Flag all set(...) calls that originate from a remote peer so the local window doesn't echo the write back over the network.

rules.quote: not assuming all writes are local
rules.rule: Don't assume all store writes are local.

rules.quote: Heavy state (entities, cells, prefab refs) flows via WebRTC after handshake, NOT in the URL.
rules.rule: Keep heavy state (entities, cells, prefab refs) out of the URL; transfer it via WebRTC after the handshake.

rules.quote: default existing panels to `mountable: {local: true, remote: false}`
rules.rule: When DockPanelDef is extended, default existing panels to mountable: {local: true, remote: false}.

rules.quote: Opt-in remotely only for panels that genuinely make sense.
rules.rule: Opt a panel into remote mountability only if it genuinely makes sense to mount remotely.

rules.quote: Document it.
rules.rule: Document last-write-wins as the conflict policy for UI state (tool, brush, selection).

rules.quote: defer that decision until concrete use cases land
rules.rule: Defer the conflict-resolution decision for richer mutations until concrete use cases land.

rules.quote: prefer the Downloads path
rules.rule: For drag-and-drop or file-input testing, prefer the ~/Downloads/Cardboard.apg path when loading a pack.

rules.quote: use the game/public/packs path
rules.rule: For URL-based pack loading, use the apps/game/public/packs/Cardboard.apg path.

rules.quote: Don't generate a new pack inside a Playwright run
rules.rule: Do not generate a new pack during a Playwright run; use the existing Cardboard.apg fixture instead.
